svg.aria-label: Differential signalling: a noise burst corrupts a single wire, but cancels out when the receiver subtracts one wire of a twisted pair from the other

ol.li: One wire, measured against the ground. A burst of interference from a nearby power cable pushes the voltage down in the middle of a 1, and the receiver reads a 0.
Use a pair of wires instead. Wire A carries the signal, and wire B carries its mirror image: when A goes up, B goes down.
The two wires are twisted tightly together, so they’re always in almost the same place. Interference pushes both of them the same way, by the same amount.
The receiver only looks at the difference between the two wires. The interference is in both, so it cancels out, and the signal comes out twice as big.

figure.figcaption: Why every network cable is made of twisted pairs.
